Purpose: Main processor — runs the pitch-detection DSP on one core and the display on the other, with PSRAM for the audio buffer and built-in Wi-Fi, BLE and USB for MIDI output.
Captures the instrument for scale detection and tuning, with a digital output that avoids any analog front-end.
Shows the detected tonic, scale and sargam, with a round format that suits the tuner dial, taal cycle and circle-of-fifths views.
Combines DAC and amplifier in one part so the processor can drive the drone and metronome click directly.
Reproduces the drone and click, sized to fit the 70mm enclosure.
Sets tempo, pitch and mode, coupled to the knurled bezel so the whole ring turns and can be adjusted by feel.
Pulses the beat so the player feels time instead of hearing it, making the metronome usable in an ensemble or under headphones.
Charges the cell over USB-C with over-charge, over-discharge and short-circuit protection.
Provides roughly 8 hours of untethered use so the device works on a music stand rather than beside an outlet.
Validate the full circuit and firmware before committing to a PCB, so design errors are caught while they cost nothing.
Prices are estimates pending cart confirmation. Multipack quantities are intentional: singles cost nearly as much, and spares mean a failed part costs an hour rather than a two-week reorder.
This is a prototype BOM. Per-unit production cost using bare modules on a custom PCB is approximately $43 CAD at quantity 5.
